activities.name: workflows#76 — remediate high-risk Python dependency vulnerabilities
activities.summary: Raised mcp to 1.28.1 and constrained joserfc/msgpack above affected versions, refreshing uv.lock (Linear POT-1931).
activities.description: Cursor-agent-driven Vanta remediation PR in potpie-ai/potpie-workflows that raises `mcp` to the fixed 1.28.1 release, constrains `joserfc` and `msgpack` above their affected versions, and regenerates `uv.lock` with secure resolved versions. Touches only `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`; verification was `uv lock --check` plus a secure-dependency smoke test constructing an MCP transport and round-tripping joserfc/msgpack. Notably the PR reports the pre-existing suite state — 109 passed, 38 failed, 45 errored — because the workflows test suite needs a configured database URL, so red pytest output is normal here and is not caused by the bump. Linked to Linear POT-1931 'Vanta potpie-ai/potpie-workflows high vulnerabilities'.

activities.name: workflows#75 — upgrade joserfc to remediate CVE-2026-48990
activities.summary: Bumped the transitive joserfc dependency 1.6.5 -> 1.7.3 to close CVE-2026-48990 (Linear POT-1934).
activities.description: Lockfile-only remediation in potpie-ai/potpie-workflows upgrading the transitive `joserfc` dependency from 1.6.5 to 1.7.3 to remediate CVE-2026-48990, which affects versions before 1.6.7. joserfc arrives through Authlib, so the fix lands purely in `uv.lock` with no `pyproject.toml` change. Verified with `uv lock --check`, a frozen install, and a joserfc/Authlib import smoke test. Filed against Linear POT-1934 'Vanta potpie-ai/potpie-workflows medium vulnerabilities'.

activities.name: workflows#74 — specs produce clearer requirement descriptions
activities.summary: Reworked the SpecGen author prompt toward outcome-first requirement prose and compact testable acceptance criteria.
activities.description: Prompt-engineering change to `src/core/agents/specgen/prompts.py` in potpie-ai/potpie-workflows that reshapes how generated specifications read. Shifts requirement descriptions toward outcome-first prose, pushes research findings toward concise synthesis, tightens acceptance criteria into compact testable checks, clarifies file-impact purpose text, and relocates deeper rationale and edge cases into guardrails, ADR, and appendix sections. The goal was reviewability: specs stayed grounded in concrete implementation details and repository evidence while becoming shorter to read. Deliberately paired with a potpie-ui spec-rendering change so the richer requirement metadata displays cleanly.

activities.name: workflows#73 — fix high and medium vulnerabilities (aiohttp, tornado)
activities.summary: Bumped aiohttp 3.14.0 -> 3.14.1 and tornado 6.5.6 -> 6.5.7 to clear five aiohttp CVEs plus GHSA-pw6j-qg29-8w7f.
activities.description: Vanta-driven dependency floor raise in potpie-ai/potpie-workflows covering aiohttp CVE-2026-54273, CVE-2026-54274, CVE-2026-54276, CVE-2026-54277 and CVE-2026-54278, plus tornado advisory GHSA-pw6j-qg29-8w7f. Only minimum version constraints in `pyproject.toml` changed (aiohttp `>=3.14.0` -> `>=3.14.1`, tornado `>=6.5.6` -> `>=6.5.7`) and `uv.lock` was regenerated via `uv lock`. This is the third aiohttp bump in this repo in two months — the same package keeps reappearing in the scanner as new advisories land on the 3.14.x line.

activities.name: workflows#72 — [Vanta] fix high vulnerabilities (starlette, cryptography, PyJWT)
activities.summary: Agent-authored Vanta high-severity sweep: starlette 1.2.1->1.3.1, python-multipart 0.0.27->0.0.32, cryptography 48->49, PyJWT 2.12.1->2.13.0.
activities.description: Opened by the Cursor GitHub App (not a human) against Linear POT-1632, this PR raises four dependency floors in potpie-ai/potpie-workflows and names the Vanta entity id for each finding — starlette `6a311e277e098647ce3afd5e`, python-multipart `6a311e277e098647ce3afd71`, cryptography `6a311e277e098647ce3afd82`, PyJWT `6a311e287e098647ce3afdb5`. Verification chain was `uv lock --check`, `uv sync --extra test`, `uv pip check`, and `uv run python -m compileall src tests`. Like its siblings it records the known-red baseline pytest result (109 passed / 38 failed / 45 errored) rather than pretending the suite is green.

activities.name: workflows#71 — [Vanta] fix low vulnerabilities (tornado 6.5.6)
activities.summary: Cursor-agent PR raising tornado from >=6.5.5 to >=6.5.6 for Vanta finding pip-tornado < 6.5.6 (POT-1604).
activities.description: Second Cursor-App-authored remediation in potpie-ai/potpie-workflows, this one clearing a low-severity Vanta finding: `pip-tornado < 6.5.6`, Vanta entity `6a2cb9507e098647ce281f14`, tracked as Linear POT-1604. Raises the direct floor from `>=6.5.5` to `>=6.5.6` and moves `uv.lock` accordingly. Verified with `uv lock --check`, `compileall`, `uv pip check`, and an import printing `tornado.version`. Six days later PR #73 bumps tornado again to 6.5.7 — a clean illustration of how fast the CVE treadmill re-fires on the same package.

activities.name: workflows#70 — medium vulnerabilities fixed (aiohttp 3.14.0, starlette 1.2.1)
activities.summary: aiohttp >=3.13.4 -> >=3.14.0 for CVE-2026-34993 / CVE-2026-47265 and starlette to >=1.0.1 for CVE-2026-48710 (BadHost).
activities.description: Medium-severity Vanta sweep in potpie-ai/potpie-workflows. aiohttp moves from `>=3.13.4` (locked 3.13.4) to `>=3.14.0` closing CVE-2026-34993 and CVE-2026-47265; starlette moves from `>=0.49.1,<1.0.0` (locked 0.50.0) to `>=1.0.1,<2.0.0` (locked 1.2.1) closing CVE-2026-48710, the BadHost host-header issue. Also touches `.gitignore`. The starlette major-version jump across the 1.0 boundary was the risky part of this change since the FastAPI rest_server surface sits directly on top of it.

activities.name: workflows#69 — medium vulnerabilities fixed (pydantic-ai floor raise)
activities.summary: Raised pydantic-ai and pydantic-ai-slim minimums from >=1.56.0 to >=1.99.0, resolving to 1.102.0.
activities.description: Dependency remediation in potpie-ai/potpie-workflows lifting both `pydantic-ai` and `pydantic-ai-slim` from `>=1.56.0` to `>=1.99.0`, with `uv.lock` resolving both to 1.102.0 so the fix also covers a later follow-up advisory. This is the highest-blast-radius bump in the CVE stream because pydantic-ai is the agent runtime underneath SpecGen, PlanGen and CodeGen — a 46-minor-version jump on the framework that drives every workflow agent, shipped as a security patch rather than a planned upgrade.

activities.name: workflows#68 — medium Vanta vulns fixed (idna >= 3.15)
activities.summary: Pinned idna>=3.15 in pyproject.toml to fix pip-idna < 3.15 / CVE-2026-45409, moving the lock from 3.10 to 3.15.
activities.description: Fixes Vanta finding `pip-idna < 3.15` / CVE-2026-45409 in potpie-ai/potpie-workflows by adding an explicit `idna>=3.15` constraint to `pyproject.toml` even though idna is purely transitive. Regenerating `uv.lock` lifted the resolved idna from 3.10 to 3.15 and forced every transitive HTTP-related dependency (requests, httpx, aiohttp chains) onto a non-vulnerable version. The pattern of pinning a transitive package directly, purely to steer the resolver, recurs repeatedly across this repo's remediation history.

activities.name: workflows#67 — high vulnerabilities solved (urllib3 >= 2.7.0)
activities.description: Follow-up to PR #66 in potpie-ai/potpie-workflows: the previous bump landed inside the still-vulnerable 2.6.x window, so this PR widens the constraint to `>=2.7.0,<3.0.0` and re-locks to urllib3 2.7.0 (was 2.6.3). CVE-2026-44432 is the decompression-bomb safeguard bypass in parts of the streaming API affecting `>=2.6.0,<2.7.0`; CVE-2026-44431 is sensitive headers being forwarded across origins on redirect. A textbook example of a remediation that had to be done twice because the first fix chose a range the advisory later swallowed.

activities.name: workflows#66 — high vulns fixed (urllib3 >= 2.6.0, first attempt)
activities.summary: First urllib3 remediation: pin moved >=2.5.0 -> >=2.6.0,<2.7.0 for CVE-2026-44432 / CVE-2026-44431.
activities.description: Initial urllib3 remediation in potpie-ai/potpie-workflows, bumping the direct pin in `pyproject.toml` from `>=2.5.0` to `>=2.6.0,<2.7.0` and running `uv lock`. It claimed to fix CVE-2026-44432 and CVE-2026-44431 but the upper bound `<2.7.0` kept the resolver inside the affected window, so the scanner re-fired and PR #67 reopened the same finding three days later. Useful as the canonical 'a CVE fix that did not actually fix the CVE' case in this repository.

activities.description: Feature-flag default flip in potpie-ai/potpie-workflows: clarifying-question generation ('QA', the Janus flow) previously defaulted to a legacy single batch and now defaults to multiple batches. Touches `src/utils/recipe_feature_flags.py`, `src/adapters/celery_recipe_streaming.py`, `src/adapters/celery_recipe_subscriber.py`, `.env_template` and `AGENTS.md`. Landing this as a default change (rather than an opt-in) is what made multi-batch Q&A the production behaviour for spec generation; the underlying implementation came from PR #57 'multi-batch structured Janus Q&A with continuation task'.

activities.name: pie#85 — test: gate Postgres migration journey
activities.summary: Adds a Postgres 16 journey driving auth, GitHub, runs and sandbox migration sets pending -> applied and replaying migrate up for idempotency.

activities.name: pie#84 — test: gate observability redaction journey

activities.name: pie#83 — test: gate platform run lifecycle journey

The gate covers Postgres, outbox processing, worker ownership, sidecar attach, Path-B tools, artifacts, event replay, cancellation, cleanup, recovery, fencing, and browser/sidecar proofs — all without invoking a live model. Motivation: the Part 8 release gate existed only inside the stacked V0 branch series, so `main` had no deterministic product-lifecycle merge gate.

activities.name: pie#82 — test: gate CLI session journey
activities.summary: Makes the CLI interactive-session test unconditional by isolating it from machine-local context state with deterministic preflight and context seams.
activities.description: Adds `.github/workflows/journey-cli-session.yml` to potpie-ai/pie. The prior test was conditionally skipped whenever a context engine was unavailable, even though the behavior under test is the CLI/orchestrator session contract rather than context retrieval. This journey introduces deterministic preflight and context seams so the real pipeline, session harness, streaming presenter, durable store, outcome, file-change reporting and usage telemetry all execute every run. Symptom it kills: a green CI that silently skipped the CLI session path.

activities.name: pie#81 — test: gate VS Code session journey
activities.summary: Turns the VS Code integration test into a required process journey with Python, uv, Bun and locked deps in one job.
activities.description: Adds `.github/workflows/journey-vscode-session.yml` to potpie-ai/pie so the editor-to-`pie serve`-to-gRPC-to-orchestrator path runs deterministically against the fake harness. The existing test could skip inside the Bun-only web job because `uv` was not installed there; this journey installs Python, uv, Bun and locked dependencies in the same job. Strengthened assertions cover event ordering, echoed text, turn completion, persisted run metadata, and the absence of error events.

activities.name: pie#80 — test: gate cross-language contract journey
activities.summary: Validates protobuf source and golden-frame consumers across Python and TypeScript in one locked CI environment so schema drift fails before merge.
activities.description: Adds `.github/workflows/journey-contracts.yml` and `./scripts/verify-journey-contracts.sh` to potpie-ai/pie. Because pie crosses Go, Python and TypeScript process boundaries, generated-code or schema drift would otherwise surface as a runtime protocol error rather than a build failure; this journey validates protobuf source and golden-frame consumers (`packages/contracts/testdata/harness_runtime_golden.jsonl`) across languages under one locked environment. Validation: 10 Python contract tests and 24 TypeScript contract tests passing.

activities.name: pie#79 — test: gate authentication session journey
activities.summary: Auth journey covering login start, idempotent retry, OIDC callback, session read, logout, cookie clearing and immediate server-side token invalidation.
activities.description: Adds `.github/workflows/journey-auth-session.yml` to potpie-ai/pie exercising login start, idempotent retry, OIDC callback, session read, already-authenticated behavior, logout, cookie clearing, and — the actual security assertion — immediate server-side invalidation of the old token. The stated reasoning is that cookie clearing alone is insufficient: a copied or delayed browser cookie must not remain a valid session after logout. Validated with `go test ./services/platform-api/internal/app -count=1 -run '^TestAuthNHTTPLoginS...'`.

activities.name: pie#78 — test: gate GitHub installation journey
activities.summary: Authenticated GitHub App journey: install start, callback, repo/branch reads, sync, disconnect, and post-disconnect not-connected assertion.
activities.description: Adds `.github/workflows/journey-github-install.yml` to potpie-ai/pie covering the full GitHub App installation flow — install start, callback with signed setup state, repository and branch reads, synchronization, disconnect, and verification that the installation is genuinely no longer connected afterward. Justified because this single user-visible integration crosses authentication, signed setup state, provider adapters, persistence and HTTP handlers, and needed one regression gate spanning all those boundaries rather than five unit tests.

activities.name: pie#77 — test: gate context engine journey

Validation: `PIE_INTEGRATION_REQUIRED=1 uv run pytest -q packages/py/orchestrator/tests/test_context_*`.

activities.name: pie#73 — V0 Part 7: Recovery and visible failure paths

The subtle design choice: deferred async turns and model egress keep running so an observer can reclaim them, instead of shutting live work down on disconnect. Recovery fixtures stay aligned with selected-ref contracts and current outbox clocks. Closes Linear POT-1973.

activities.name: pie#71 — V0 Part 6: Tool coordination and pie-harness
activities.summary: Integrates the TypeScript pie-harness sidecar with the Go NDJSON runtime and adds the Path-B tool poll/result loop with fenced ToolCoordinator execution (POT-1969).

activities.name: pie#74 — VS Code / pie serve Langfuse turn tracing
activities.summary: Links pie.vscode.turn to pie.turn via W3C traceparent on SendTurn and adds Pi sidecar gen_ai.chat spans with prompt/response capture.

activities.name: pie#72 — SDK redaction and collector verification

activities.name: pie#87 — VS Code onboarding UI and chat UI

Search terms: pi sidecar open times out, Bun stdin pipe EOF, PTY workaround, VS Code onboarding, harness picker.

activities.name: workflows f9a4e4e — rework spec generation around deep agents
activities.summary: Replaced the six-step SpecGen pipeline with a two-phase deep-agent design (research then author).
activities.description: The architectural pivot of SpecGen in potpie-ai/potpie-workflows: the previous six-step deterministic pipeline is torn out and replaced by a two-phase deep-agent flow — a research phase that explores the repository, then an author phase that writes the specification. Landed on branch new-spec-deep-agent and shipped through PR #55. The same branch immediately followed up in 581c5fc by giving the hybrid research agent real filesystem tools — Potpie read/grep/glob/bash, with grep executed via ripgrep — so spec research became repository-grounded rather than embedding-only. Everything under src/core/agents/specgen/ descends from this commit, including the prompt tuning later done in PR #74. Search terms: deep agent, specgen rework, research then author, two-phase pipeline, ripgrep research tools.
